page_objective: Define how SIPANEL communicates engineering expertise through structured storytelling that explains technical problems, envelope-system logic, execution control, and measurable industrial outcomes across sandwich panels, aluminum cladding, ZIP roofing, and industrial building envelope systems.

storytelling_philosophy.statement: SIPANEL storytelling should educate, clarify, and build trust through engineering thinking rather than promotional marketing language.

primary_storytelling_goals.description: Demonstrate engineering expertise through structured explanation, system logic, and execution control.
Help industrial clients understand technical risks and solutions across roofing, cladding, sandwich panel, and envelope systems without overwhelming detail.
Use engineering clarity and measurable proof to reduce project hesitation and guide users toward qualified consultation.

primary_storytelling_goals.goal: Position SIPANEL as an Industrial Envelope Partner
primary_storytelling_goals.description: Avoid sandwich-panel-only positioning by communicating capability across sandwich panels, aluminum cladding, ZIP roofing, and envelope coordination.

step_1.title: Industrial Context
step_1.purpose: Establish the project environment, industry type, operational conditions, and envelope system category.
required_content: Relevant system category: sandwich panel, aluminum cladding, ZIP roofing, or mixed envelope

step_2.title: Engineering Problem
step_2.purpose: Clearly explain the technical challenge, risk, or execution issue.

step_3.title: Technical Analysis
step_3.purpose: Demonstrate engineering reasoning, root-cause logic, and system evaluation.

step_4.title: SIPANEL Engineering Approach
step_4.purpose: Present the technical strategy and engineered solution.

step_5.title: Execution Process
step_5.purpose: Show implementation discipline, technical workflow, and execution control.

rules: Start with the engineering problem, not the product.
Explain technical reasoning clearly.
Use practical industrial examples.
Focus on execution quality and risk reduction.
Connect every solution to measurable value.
Represent SIPANEL as an industrial envelope engineering partner, not only a sandwich panel provider.
Match the narrative to the correct system category: sandwich panel, aluminum cladding, ZIP roofing, or mixed envelope system.
Avoid forcing roof waterproofing language into façade or cladding stories when it is not technically relevant.
Use plain engineering language where possible.
Break complex systems into smaller explanations.
Support explanations with diagrams and visuals.
Avoid unnecessary jargon overload.
Preserve technical accuracy.
Explain façade attachment logic when discussing cladding systems.
Explain standing seam movement behavior when discussing ZIP roofing.
Support thermal bridge analysis with simple diagrams.
Explain envelope transition conditions clearly.
Use consultant-level terminology where needed, but explain it for broader industrial audiences.

requirements: Every engineering story must include proof.
Use system-specific proof for sandwich panels, aluminum cladding, ZIP roofing, and envelope systems.
Support cladding narratives with façade details and execution photography.
Support ZIP roofing narratives with standing seam sections and movement logic.
Support envelope narratives with transition diagrams and mixed-system case studies.

rules: Use strong section hierarchy.
Keep paragraphs concise.
Use bullets for technical detail.
Maintain mobile readability.
Separate explanation from proof visually.
Use system labels where needed to clarify whether the story is about sandwich panels, cladding, ZIP roofing, or envelope coordination.
Avoid mixing too many technical systems in one section unless the story is specifically about envelope integration.
Visuals should explain engineering logic.
Avoid decorative imagery.
Use annotations carefully.
Keep visuals technically relevant.
Use façade visuals for cladding stories.
Use seam and movement details for ZIP roofing stories.
Use transition diagrams for envelope coordination stories.
Align storytelling with industrial search intent.
Use technical keywords naturally.
Structure stories for scannability.
Support long-tail engineering searches.
Use cladding, façade, standing seam, ZIP roofing, and envelope terminology on relevant pages.
Do not use one roofing-focused narrative template for every SEO page.
Use engineering clarity to reduce hesitation.
Place CTA after proof sections.
Use consultation-focused CTA language.
Support CTA with measurable trust.
Match CTA language to the system category and story context.

mobile: Break technical sections into accordions when needed.
Use one system focus per viewport where possible.
Avoid stacking too many technical systems in one mobile section.
desktop: Use split layouts for problem-analysis-solution storytelling.
Allow larger diagrams for façade, standing seam, and envelope transition explanations.

requirements: Provide alt text for all visuals.
Keep technical explanations readable for assistive technologies.
Provide accessible summaries for diagrams explaining cladding, ZIP roofing, and envelope transitions.

rules: Preserve storytelling flow across languages.
Maintain engineering terminology consistency.
Allow layout adaptation for translated content.
Mirror directional diagrams where necessary.
Validate façade, cladding, ZIP roofing, and envelope terminology in every supported language.
Keep technical abbreviations such as ACP, ZIP, CAD, BOM, MTO, and RFQ consistent where appropriate.

qa_checklist: The system category is clear: sandwich panel, aluminum cladding, ZIP roofing, or envelope engineering.
The story does not position SIPANEL as sandwich-panel-only.
Cladding and ZIP roofing terminology is accurate where used.
Technical visuals match the story topic.
forbidden_patterns: Missing façade or cladding context on relevant pages
Using the same story structure for all systems without technical adaptation
implementation_notes: Engineering storytelling is a core SIPANEL differentiation strategy.
Stories must educate and build trust through technical clarity and measurable execution quality.
Every engineering narrative should connect problem, analysis, execution, and proof.
Storytelling systems should integrate with SEO, case studies, conversion flows, and technical resource content.
Storytelling must represent SIPANEL as an industrial envelope engineering partner across sandwich panels, aluminum cladding, ZIP roofing, and coordinated envelope systems.
